odds-refresh.caveats: UNIFORM SNAPSHOT: all 8 boards were captured in a single ~20-minute window, 2026-06-10 18:44-19:05 UTC (evening before the 06-12 02:00 UTC opener; no matches played). Book-level timestamps: Caesars 18:47, DraftKings 18:52, BetMGM 18:55, FanDuel 19:00 (all via BettingPros API 'updated' stamps), Pinnacle ~18:55, Kalshi 18:57, Betfair Exchange ~19:05, Polymarket trades 18:44-18:54 UTC. CONVERSIONS: retail/Pinnacle American odds converted as decimal=1+A/100; Polymarket decimal=1/last-trade price; Kalshi decimal=1/midpoint of yes bid/ask; Betfair=best available back price (decimal native). Per-team consensus decimal_odds = MEDIAN of available books (mixes vigged retail with low-margin exchange/prediction prices; retail 48-outcome overround is roughly 120-135%, so de-vig before using as probabilities - prefer Pinnacle/Betfair/Polymarket for calibration). GAPS: (1) bet365 board NOT obtained - bet365, oddschecker, vegasinsider, legalsportsreport and direct DK/MGM/FanDuel/Caesars sites all bot-blocked; only a stale 2026-06-05 partial bet365 list exists in secondary sources and was excluded. (2) DraftKings and Caesars carry no Turkey price in the BettingPros feed (47/48 teams; Turkey covered by the other 6 books). (3) Kalshi longshot markets are thin with wide spreads (bid often $0.000): the 200.0 values for Iraq, DR Congo, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Czech Republic are bid/ask-midpoint artifacts of a $0.01 ask and overstate true probability; treat Kalshi (and to a lesser degree Polymarket) tails below ~1% as unreliable. (4) Betfair Exchange tail prices cluster at 1000 (site max back quote, little/no lay liquidity). (5) Betfair Exchange quotes are pre-commission (2-5% on net winnings). VALIDATION: BetMGM column exactly matches Yahoo's independent 2026-06-10 full board; DraftKings column exactly matches CBS Sports' 2026-06-10 update; Kalshi matches Covers' 2026-06-10 12:11 ET snapshot within 0.2pp. Spain/France market order flipped vs some June-3-5 boards (England 700->750 at DK), confirming this is the fresher line.

backtest-structures.caveats: 1) Teams in each group are listed in FINAL group-standings order (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th), parsed from the rendered standings tables of the Wikipedia main articles; 1st/2nd advanced to the R16. 2) Official FIFA match numbers were taken from the two official FIFA match-schedule PDFs (both cited as the 'match schedule' reference in the Wikipedia knockout-stage articles), since Wikipedia's knockout pages do not print match numbers. Both years share the identical bracket: R16 49=1Av2B, 50=1Cv2D, 51=1Bv2A, 52=1Dv2C, 53=1Ev2F, 54=1Gv2H, 55=1Fv2E, 56=1Hv2G; QF 57=W49vW50, 58=W53vW54, 59=W51vW52, 60=W55vW56; SF 61=W57vW58, 62=W59vW60; 63=3rd place (losers 61/62), 64=final. Note match numbers are not strictly chronological within a day (e.g. 2018 M49 kicked off after M50; 2022 M52 before M51, M58 before M57, M60 before M59). 3) Discrepancy found and resolved: fixturedownload.com's 2018 CSV swaps QF numbers 59/60 (lists 59=Sweden-England, 60=Russia-Croatia) relative to the official FIFA PDF (59=W51vW52=Russia-Croatia at Sochi, 60=W55vW56=Sweden-England at Samara); the FIFA PDF was used as authoritative. An initial an automated fetch summary of the 2022 Wikipedia page also mis-assigned 51/52 and 57/58; the FIFA PDF settled these. 4) The current Wikipedia revisions contain no separate 'final standings/ranking' table, so stage_reached was double-checked against the verified group standings tables (3rd/4th = groups) plus the full knockout brackets extracted from the knockout-stage article wikitext (R16/QF losers, SF losers incl. 3rd-place participants, final loser, champion); counts per tournament are 1+1+2+4+8+16=32. 5) 'sf' includes both semifinal losers regardless of third-place match outcome (2018: Belgium 3rd, England 4th; 2022: Croatia 3rd, Morocco 4th). 6) Home/away order in r16_pairings follows the official FIFA designation (group winner listed first).

elo-methodology.goal_diff_multiplier: Rating change = K x G x (W - We), where G scales K by margin of victory. Exact rule from eloratings.net/about: "K is then adjusted for the goal difference in the game. It is increased by half if a game is won by two goals, by 3/4 if a game is won by three goals, and by 3/4 + (N-3)/8 if the game is won by four or more goals, where N is the goal difference." Equivalently (Wikipedia form): G = 1 for a draw or 1-goal win; G = 3/2 for a 2-goal win; G = (11+N)/8 for N >= 3 (3 goals -> 1.75, 4 -> 1.875, 5 -> 2.0, 6 -> 2.125, +0.125 per extra goal). Empirically verified: Georgia 0-4 Spain (WCQ 2025-11-15): K=40, G=1.875, We(GE)=0.092 -> 40*1.875*(0-0.092) = -6.9, matches the published -7.
elo-methodology.draw_handling: W = 1 for a win, 0.5 for a draw, 0 for a loss; this includes wins/losses in extra time (counted as full wins/losses). Expected result We = 1 / (10^(-dr/400) + 1) with dr = difference in ratings plus 100 points for the team playing at home (no addition on neutral ground; eloratings.net match data records neutral venues explicitly). A draw therefore moves ratings by K x G x (0.5 - We): the higher-rated side loses points, the lower-rated side gains them. Example verified: Spain 2-2 Turkey (WCQ 2025-11-18) cost Spain 17 points (2189 -> 2172).
elo-methodology.shootout_handling: Matches decided by a penalty shootout are scored as DRAWS (W = 0.5 for both teams), using the score at the end of extra time; the shootout result itself is ignored. Source: Wikipedia "World Football Elo Ratings" (Result of match section): "If the match is decided on penalties, however, the result of the game is considered a draw (W = 0.5)" — explicitly contrasted with the post-2018 FIFA Elo-based ranking, which counts shootouts as win/loss. Empirically verified in eloratings.net data: 2025-06-08 UEFA Nations League final Portugal 2-2 Spain (Portugal won on penalties) was settled as a draw: Portugal +10 (2020->2030), Spain -10 (2167->2157), consistent with K=50, W=0.5, We(PT)=0.30 on neutral ground.
elo-methodology.caveats: 1) ARCHIVED World.tsv DOES NOT EXIST FOR 2018/2022: Wayback CDX shows only two captures of https://www.eloratings.net/World.tsv, both from 2026 (20260506122444, 20260604022542); the suggested URL web.archive.org/web/20180610/.../World.tsv silently redirects to the 2026-05-06 capture. Workaround used: (a) contemporaneous Wayback captures of the Wikipedia article (2018-06-08 capture, table labeled "as they were on 5 June 2018", full top 100; 2022-11-13 capture, table labeled "Top 20 rankings as of 26 October 2022" - by 2022 the article carried only a top-20 table); (b) eloratings.net's own per-tournament pre-tournament files 2018_World_Cup_start.tsv / 2022_World_Cup_start.tsv (ratings immediately before each tournament's first match; menu.tsv dates them 2018-06-13 and 2022-11-19), retrieved live 2026-06-10 and saved to the Wayback Machine the same day (capture timestamps 20260610191155 / 20260610191208 - capture date is 2026, content is the official start-of-tournament ratings). These start files cover ALL 32 participants of both tournaments with zero gaps. 2) The 2022-11-13 Wikipedia snapshot covers only 15 of 32 participants (missing: Qatar, Senegal, Iran, United States, Wales, Mexico, Poland, Saudi Arabia, Australia, Tunisia, Japan, Costa Rica, Canada, Morocco, Cameroon, Ghana, South Korea); its values are pre-November-friendlies (no matches were played 2022-09-28..2022-11-15, so they equal mid-November ratings for teams that did not play Nov 16-19 warm-ups). 3) Differences between the 2018-06-05 Wikipedia table and the 2018-06-13 start file are explained by June 8-13 friendlies (e.g. France 1995->1986 after 1-1 vs USA; Brazil 2136->2141 after 3-0 vs Austria); a residual 1-2 pt discrepancy for a few teams that played no match (e.g. Argentina 1986 vs 1984) indicates eloratings.net retroactively revises historical data slightly - prefer the start files for modeling consistency. In the 2018 snapshot parse, displayed ranks for Uruguay/Australia/Tunisia rows had non-standard markup, so only ratings (verified against intervening results) are reported. 4) K FOR NATIONS LEAGUE is not named on eloratings.net/about; the values given (league phase 40, Finals/knockouts 50) are empirical back-computations from published per-match rating exchanges (marked EMPIRICAL in k_factors) and were exact to rounding in every checked match. 5) The about-page text is served as https://www.eloratings.net/about.tsv (the /about URL is a JS shell); the about page itself never mentions shootouts - the shootout-as-draw rule comes from the Wikipedia description and was verified empirically (2025 Nations League final). 6) SPAIN PEAK: live World.tsv (retrieved 2026-06-10) shows Spain current 2157 (rank 1) with all-time-best columns rank 1 / rating 2189; match-level 2025 data pins the 2189 peak to 2025-11-15 (Georgia 0-4 Spain, WC qualifier), receding to 2172 after the 2-2 draw with Turkey on 2025-11-18. So 2157 is 32 pts below Spain's own all-time high. It is NOT near the cross-nation all-time record: live site high-water columns show Hungary 2234, Germany 2223, England 2213, Brazil 2195; the June-2018 Wikipedia snapshot's "highest ever" table similarly listed Hungary 2230, Germany 2223, England 2216, Brazil 2194, Spain 2165, Argentina 2159 (small deltas vs today's site = retroactive revisions). Hungary's peak is conventionally dated to mid-1954, but I did not independently verify peak dates for nations other than Spain. 7) Formula note: the site writes the update as Rn = Ro + K(W-We) with K "adjusted" by the goal-difference factor, i.e. effective change = K x G x (W - We) with K from k_factors and G from goal_diff_multiplier; ratings are published rounded to integers, and the home +100 is applied only inside dr (not added on neutral ground; the 2025 Nations League Finals matches in Germany verify neutral-venue handling).
